Clinical relevance (MCID) zones

Source: R/geom-mcid-zones.R
geom_mcid_zones.Rd

Draws "harm", "trivial" and "benefit" background zones defined by a minimal clinically important difference (MCID) behind estimates and confidence intervals. The thresholds may be asymmetric and uncertain (given as ranges). The layer draws a reference background only: it does not classify estimates or compute the probability that an effect is beneficial.

Usage

geom_mcid_zones(
  mcid,
  sd = NULL,
  null = 0,
  softness = NULL,
  beyond = c("flat", "multiples"),
  palette = "diverging",
  alpha = 0.35,
  orientation = "x",
  expand = FALSE,
  labels = FALSE,
  label_size = 3,
  label_colour = "grey20",
  n_slices = 40,
  title = NULL,
  show.legend = NA,
  ...
)

Arguments

mcid

An mcid_thresholds() object, or a bare positive number (symmetric shorthand for mcid_thresholds(mcid = x), with higher values better).

sd

If given, thresholds are divided by sd, for an axis that shows standardised differences.

null

Position of the null on the axis.

softness

NULL (hard edges unless the MCID is a range) or a fraction of each point threshold over which to fade.

beyond

"flat" (default): one colour beyond the MCID. "multiples": deepening colour at 2x and 3x the MCID.

palette

"diverging" (default), "grey", or three colours.

alpha

Opacity of the fills.

orientation

The axis that shows the effect: "x" (default, as in forest plots) or "y".

expand

If TRUE, all zone boundaries train the position scale.

labels

If TRUE, zone names are printed inside the panel, near the top (effect on the horizontal axis) or the right edge (vertical axis).

label_size, label_colour

Size (mm) and colour of zone labels.

n_slices

Number of thin rectangles used to draw each soft transition.

title

Legend title. Defaults to the short source of the thresholds.

show.legend

Should the zone legend be shown?

...

Other arguments passed to ggplot2::layer().

Value

An object that can be added to a ggplot with +.

Details

Add the layer before points, error bars and reference lines so that they are drawn on top of the zones.

Where the MCID comes from

An MCID should come from patients' judgements (anchor-based methods; Jaeschke, Singer & Guyatt 1989). Distribution-based values, created only through an explicit call to mcid_distribution(), are marked provisional and the legend says so. There is no automatic MCID.

The MCID is usually defined for change within a patient, whereas contrasts between groups are differences in mean outcome. Reading group differences against an MCID is common but contested; see vignette("effectzones").

Boundaries

With softness = NULL (default) boundaries are hard edges, except where the MCID was given as a range: the background then fades from one zone to the next across that range, showing where the threshold is uncertain. A number gives soft transitions spanning that fraction of each point threshold.

With beyond = "multiples" the colour keeps deepening at 2 and 3 times the MCID (capped at 3), so that an estimate at 1.2 x MCID and one at 4 x MCID sit on visibly different backgrounds. Multiples are of the midpoint when the MCID is a range.

Palettes

The default "diverging" palette uses muted blue (benefit) and orange (harm), which remain distinguishable under the common colour-vision deficiencies, around a neutral centre. The "grey" palette uses white for trivial and two clearly different greys for benefit and harm. Grey levels carry no natural direction, so use labels = TRUE with it (or make sure the legend is printed) so readers can tell which side is which. A custom palette is three colours named harm, trivial, benefit.

References

Jaeschke R, Singer J, Guyatt GH (1989). Measurement of health status: ascertaining the minimal clinically important difference. Controlled Clinical Trials 10(4):407-415. doi:10.1016/0197-2456(89)90005-6

McGlothlin AE, Lewis RJ (2014). Minimal clinically important difference: defining what really matters to patients. JAMA 312(13):1342-1343.

See also

mcid_thresholds(), mcid_distribution(), geom_es_zones()

Examples

library(ggplot2)
df <- data.frame(term = c("Dose 1", "Dose 2", "Dose 3"),
                 estimate = c(2, 6, 11), lower = c(-3, 1, 5),
                 upper = c(7, 11, 17))

ggplot(df, aes(estimate, term)) +
  geom_mcid_zones(mcid_thresholds(lower = -4, upper = c(5, 8))) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper), width = 0.2) +
  geom_point() +
  theme_minimal()


# Grey palette: label the zones
ggplot(df, aes(estimate, term)) +
  geom_mcid_zones(5, palette = "grey", labels = TRUE) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper), width = 0.2) +
  geom_point()
